_comment: Retired politician_id → canonical politician_id. `politician_id` is free text across the vr_* tables (there is no politicians table and no FK), so the same person can end up under two ids — a curated seed using one and the live ingest another. When a merge migration folds one id into another, record the retirement here: the ingest canonicalizes on write and the Voting Record API canonicalizes on read, so a stale Blobs member-map override, an old bookmark, or a saved client record can never re-open the split. Client-side stance lookups have their own bridge (STANCE_ALIASES in stance-helpers.js) — keep the two in step.

notes.susan_collins: Susan Collins (R-ME, C001035). Merged by netlify/database/migrations/20260725050000_vr_merge_susan_collins_identity.sql. `collins` is canonical: it is the cmp-data.js roster id, carries the richer sourced stance block, and held 19 of her 22 roll-call votes.
notes.kennedy_rfk: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. (HHS Secretary). No merge migration: he holds NO DB rows under either id — 0 in vr_member_votes, 0 in vr_positions, 0 pdx_proposals links (verified against the branch DB, July 25 2026) — because a cabinet officer casts no roll-call votes. This was a curated-content split, not a vote split, so it was fixed in the data files: the six sourced stance cards moved into the `rfkjr` block in politician-stances.js, the duplicate cmp-data.js roster record was removed, and the one spotlight card was re-keyed. `rfkjr` is canonical: it carries every deep-dive surface (cmp-data-detail.js, spotlight-cards-data.js, acct-spotlight-data.js, the index.html votingRecords block and profile blurb), the repaired official portrait, termStart tenure, and 3 of the 4 spotlight cards. The alias still matters even with no rows: the ingest canonicalizes on write and the Voting Record API on read, so if a future source ever attributes a row to `kennedy_rfk` it lands on `rfkjr` instead of re-opening the split.
notes.cullimore_s19: Kirk A. Cullimore Jr. (R, Utah State Senate; Senate Majority Leader since Jan 21 2025). ONE person under two ids, and the districts in the two records were not a contradiction but a timeline: he was elected in 2018 to Utah Senate District 9, and the post-2020-census redistricting renumbered his Salt Lake County seat to District 19 effective Jan 1 2023 (Wikipedia/Ballotpedia; his own campaign site still prints the old number). District 9 is now held by a DIFFERENT senator, Jen Plumb (D-Salt Lake City) — already in the roster as `jen_plumb_s9` — so the stale `kcullimore` label was actively attributing another member's district to him. No merge migration: he holds NO DB rows under either id — 0 in vr_member_votes, 0 in vr_positions, 0 pdx_proposals links (verified against the branch DB, July 25 2026), as the vr_* tables carry congressional roll calls and he is a state legislator. Fixed in the data files instead: the duplicate cmp-data.js roster record was removed after its district was corrected to 19, the `cullimore_s19` bio was folded into the `kcullimore` cmp-data-detail.js record, and the ballot/incumbent references were re-keyed. `kcullimore` is canonical: it carries the promise score (14 kept / 6 broken / 5 pending), the real detail stances, the official le.utah.gov portrait, the profile blurb, both spotlight layers (spotlight-cards-data.js and acct-spotlight-data.js), four deep-dive script surfaces, and index.html's ACCT_ALIAS already pointed `cullimore_s19` at it. Curated stance cards stay under the name-slug key `kirk_cullimore` per this file's stance-key convention; STANCE_ALIASES bridges both ids to it.
